android_fork_merge.notes: Deep sync of the fork with upstream horizon-rust/horizon:main as of 2026-11-15. The fork keeps: Compose/JNI launcher, ARM64 Rust build with the Android touch stack, .hmod/.hnmod native-mod pipeline, Android renderer preparation machinery (deferred background renderer build, recreate_surface on resume, GL-blocking guards), per-instance presets, and the Android workflows. Upstream's crate split (horizon-client-lib, horizon-hooks, horizon-official, horizon-optifine, etc.) and NATIVE_HOOKS_API 645 are adopted. Gameplay now lives in the library, so JNI/activity code stays in horizon-android and the library reaches the platform through a host table it installs once (crates/horizon-client/src/android_host.rs; device_runtime::Frame records the frame on drop). The launcher files the bridge shares are compiled through launcher/src/android_shared.rs (the launcher needs GPUI, so it cannot be a crate dependency); their backend resolves game paths to the app home on Android. Upstream stopped running WebAssembly code mods, so the fork's mod-menu runtime hooks are documented no-ops; the .hnmod native-mod path is unchanged. Native Android checks build arm64 only (.github/workflows/android-source.yml and packaging/android/source-checks.yml stay byte-identical). Deployment workflows remain disabled under .github/upstream-workflows/. Two fork-only fixes ride along: the catalog now calls a native mod "Built" only when the chosen build's build.json lists it (a source .hnmod alone is not installed), and the launcher's build server defaults to this fork's deployed Worker (https://horizon-mod-builds.steve-horizon-android-hnmod.workers.dev), so Build actually sends the enabled .hnmod files. PR #13 merged into android at 2fde1b23b5. Post-merge fixes (#14, branch fix/android-gles-and-warnings, commit d11096cc0d09bc989c6dc858e57de86986504843): the dev 29 APK crashed on the OpenGL ES renderer because the GLES emissive unroller still matched the old 32-entry loop while the synced terrain.wgsl has 128; terrain.wgsl also declared both the fork's packed TerrainOut entry points and upstream's TerrainWire ones, so both backends rejected the module, and the GLES module lacked the hdr_light.wgsl prelude. The fork now keeps the upstream wire interface and lowers it for GLES, unrolls all 128 entries without panicking when the shader changes, and disables the Android static-cutout/settled-terrain pipelines until they get a wire-interface fragment. Game::options_to_game is restored with the pre-removal Done behavior so native mods written before upstream removed the HDR shortcut compile again. The build warnings are fixed across horizon-client, horizon-client-render, horizon-android and the shared launcher backend; actions/setup-java is v5 in both identical workflow copies.
